questions.question: The term "Amaram" in Vijayanagara administration was associated with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Military fief**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Amaram** in the Vijayanagara administration referred to a **military fief**, which means a land grant assigned to commanders or military officers in place of their services.
 
• The **Amaram** system was primarily utilized to organize and maintain a strong military structure in the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Under this system, the Amara Nayakas (military commanders) were given land grants called "Amaram," and in return, they had to maintain a specified number of troops ready for the empire's defense or campaigns.
 
• The Amara Nayakas had administrative control over the land and were allowed to collect revenue from it, which was then used to fund their military obligations.
 
• This system played a crucial role in decentralizing the military and administrative responsibilities, ensuring effective governance across the vast Vijayanagara Empire.

• The Vijayanagara Empire was established in **1336 CE** by **Harihara I** and **Bukka Raya I**. It was one of the most powerful South Indian kingdoms.
 
• The empire is renowned for its contributions to **art, architecture**, and **administration**, as well as its ability to maintain a strong military.
 
• The capital city of the empire was **Hampi**, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Amara Nayaka System:**
 
 
• This system was inspired by the **Iqta system** of the Delhi Sultanate but was adapted to suit the needs of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Amara Nayakas were responsible for **revenue collection**, **maintenance of law and order**, and providing military support to the central authority.
 
• They acted as intermediaries between the central government and the local population.
 
 
 
• **Other Administrative Systems:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagara administration was highly decentralized, with a well-organized structure involving provincial governors and local chieftains.
 
• The empire also maintained a detailed system of land measurement and revenue collection.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Systems:**

• Land redistribution was not a significant feature of the Vijayanagara administration, but was seen in later agrarian reforms in India.
 
• Merchant guilds, such as the **Ayyavole** and **Manigramam**, operated independently of the Amaram system and were primarily focused on trade and commerce.

__
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was established in **1983** by the Government of India to examine and review the working of the existing arrangements between the **Centre and the States** regarding legislative, administrative, and financial relations.
 
• It aimed at ensuring proper functioning of the Indian federal system. The commission was chaired by **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**, a retired Supreme Court judge.
 
• The commission submitted its report in **1988**, making **over 247 recommendations** to improve Centre-State relations.
 
• Key recommendations included the **appointment of Governors**, the role of the **Rajya Sabha**, and the need for greater cooperation between the Centre and States for better governance.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the importance of cooperative federalism and suggested mechanisms to resolve disputes between the Centre and the States.

• **Punchhi Commission:**

 
 
• The **Punchhi Commission** was established in **2007** to further review Centre-State relations and address emerging challenges.
 
• It emphasized the need for maintaining a balance of power and provided recommendations on issues such as **internal security, public order, and socio-economic planning**.
 
• The commission submitted its report in **2010**, suggesting reforms in the **appointment of Governors, emergency provisions, and financial relations**.
 
 
 
• **Ashok Mehta Committee:**
 
 
• The **Ashok Mehta Committee** was set up in **1977** to recommend measures for strengthening the **Panchayati Raj system**.
 
• It proposed the establishment of a **two-tier system** of Panchayati Raj, consisting of Mandal Panchayats and Zilla Parishads.
 
• Its recommendations were aimed at decentralizing power and empowering local self-governance, rather than addressing Centre-State relations.
 
 
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:**

• It recommended the establishment of the **three-tier Panchayati Raj system**: Village Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zilla Parishad.
 
• The committee's focus was on local governance, not Centre-State relations.

questions.question: The "Vallamkali" boat races of Kerala feature which unique type of boat, known for its length and speed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chundan Vallam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "Vallamkali" or boat races of Kerala are an integral part of the state's culture and tradition, primarily conducted during the festival of **Onam**.
 
• **Chundan Vallam**, also known as the **Snake Boat**, is the unique type of boat featured in these races. These boats are famous for their extraordinary **length, speed, and sleek design**.
 
• Chundan Vallam boats are characterized by their impressive length, often measuring **100 to 138 feet**, and can hold around **100 to 150 rowers**.
 
• These boats are traditionally crafted from the wood of the **Anjili tree (Artocarpus hirsutus)**, a durable and water-resistant material.
 
• The races are highly competitive and are accompanied by traditional songs known as **Vanchipattu**, which boost the morale of the rowers and add to the festive atmosphere.
 
• Chundan Vallam holds a historical significance as these boats were originally designed as **war boats** by the local rulers of Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Types of Vallam (Boats):**

 
 
• **Odi Vallam**: A smaller racing boat used in local races but not as prominent as Chundan Vallam.
 
• **Iruttukuthi Vallam**: Known for its speed, it is smaller in size compared to Chundan Vallam.
 
• **Churulan Vallam**: A smaller and round-shaped boat used for racing in some regions of Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Vallamkali:**
 
 
• The boat races are deeply rooted in Kerala's history, serving as a symbol of unity and teamwork among the participants.
 
• It is not just a sporting event but also a **spiritual offering** to the deities, often conducted at temple festivals.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Chundan Vallam:**
 
 
• The prow of the boat is raised high, resembling the hood of a snake, hence the name **Snake Boat**.
 
• It is manned by a synchronized team of rowers, steered by a **chief oarsman**, and accompanied by a group of singers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Chundan Vallam was historically used as a war vessel to transport soldiers and goods, showcasing its robust design and utility.
 
 
 
• **Nehru Trophy Boat Race:**
 
 
• Named after India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who visited Kerala in 1952 and was fascinated by the Snake Boat races.
 
• This annual race is among the most prestigious Vallamkali events.

questions.question: The Bhimakali Temple in Sarahan is a fine example of which architectural style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kath-Kuni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhimakali Temple** in Sarahan, Himachal Pradesh, is a remarkable example of the **Kath-Kuni architectural style**.
 
• **Kath-Kuni** is an indigenous architectural style of the **Himalayan region**, particularly popular in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The style prominently uses **wood and stone**, arranged alternately in layers, which gives the structure strength and makes it resistant to earthquakes.
 
• The Bhimakali Temple showcases the usage of **deodar wood** and stone, both of which are abundantly available in the region, making it environmentally sustainable and culturally significant.
 
• This architectural style is known for its **intricate carvings, sloping roofs, and stacked construction technique**, which also offers excellent insulation against the cold climate of the Himalayas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kath-Kuni Architectural Style:**

 
 
• The term "Kath-Kuni" derives from two words in the local dialect: **"Kath," meaning wood**, and **"Kuni," meaning corner**.
 
• This technique is widely used in **temples, houses, and forts** across Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
 
• It provides **structural flexibility**, which is crucial in earthquake-prone areas like the Himalayan region.
 
• The structures often feature **flat roofs or pagoda-style roofs** made of slate, which helps in dealing with heavy snowfall.
 
 
 
• **Bhimakali Temple:**
 
 
• The Bhimakali Temple is a **900-year-old structure** and an important religious and architectural landmark in Sarahan.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Goddess Bhimakali**, the presiding deity of the rulers of the former Bushahr state.
 
• The temple complex comprises multiple shrines, with the main temple reflecting traditional **Kath-Kuni construction methods**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Styles:**
 
 
• **Chalukyan Style:** Predominantly seen in South India, featuring intricately carved temple spires and stone construction. *This is not related to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
• **Dravidian Style:** Characterized by towering gopurams (gateway towers) and richly decorated stone carvings, common in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. *This does not apply to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
• **Indo-Gothic Style:** A colonial architectural style combining Indian and Gothic elements, primarily seen in buildings constructed during British rule. *This is unrelated to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve the **Kath-Kuni architecture** as it represents the cultural heritage of the Himalayan region.
 
• Initiatives include workshops and training programs for local artisans to keep the tradition alive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Kath-Kuni:**

 
 
• It is a **climate-responsive construction style**, offering natural insulation and durability.
 
• The use of **local materials** reduces the environmental impact and promotes sustainability.

questions.question: Which Chinese-American author's novel "The Joy Luck Club" became internationally acclaimed and adapted into a film in 1993?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amy Tan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amy Tan, a renowned **Chinese-American author**, wrote the acclaimed novel **"The Joy Luck Club"**, published in **1989**. The book garnered critical and commercial success worldwide.
 
• "The Joy Luck Club" explores the lives and relationships of **Chinese immigrant mothers** and their **Chinese-American daughters**, portraying themes of cultural identity, generational conflict, and familial bonds.
 
• The novel was adapted into a film in **1993**, directed by **Wayne Wang**. The movie received widespread praise and was one of the first mainstream Hollywood films to feature a predominantly Asian cast.
 
• Amy Tan's writing often reflects her personal experiences as the daughter of Chinese immigrants, addressing the challenges of balancing traditional values with contemporary American culture.
 
• The novel's success established Amy Tan as one of the leading voices in **Asian-American literature**, contributing significantly to the representation of Asian-American stories in mainstream media.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About "The Joy Luck Club":**

 
 
• The novel is structured as a series of interconnected stories, offering perspectives from eight characters—four mothers and their daughters. Each story delves into the characters' struggles with their cultural heritage and personal aspirations.
 
• The title refers to a **mahjong club** formed by the immigrant mothers to maintain their cultural ties and share their experiences in America.
 
• The themes of the book include **cultural identity**, **mother-daughter relationships**, and the complexities of assimilation into a new culture.
 
 
 
• **Amy Tan's Other Works:**
 
 
• After the success of "The Joy Luck Club," Amy Tan wrote other acclaimed novels such as **"The Kitchen God's Wife"** (1991), **"The Hundred Secret Senses"** (1995), and **"The Bonesetter's Daughter"** (2001).
 
• Her works often explore themes of **family, identity, and cultural heritage**, drawing heavily from her own experiences and background.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation of "The Joy Luck Club":**
 
 
• The 1993 film adaptation was groundbreaking for its **representation of Asian-American characters** in Hollywood, paving the way for future projects like **"Crazy Rich Asians"** (2018).
 
• The screenplay was co-written by **Amy Tan** and **Ronald Bass**, ensuring the film remained faithful to the novel's themes and narratives.
 
 
 
• **Other Authors from the Options:**
 
 
• **Celeste Ng:** Author of **"Little Fires Everywhere"** and **"Everything I Never Told You"**. Her works explore family dynamics and social issues but are unrelated to "The Joy Luck Club."
 
• **Maxine Hong Kingston:** Known for **"The Woman Warrior"** and **"China Men"**, Kingston's works focus on Chinese-American identity but are distinct from Amy Tan's storytelling style.
 
• **Lisa See:** Famous for novels like **"Snow Flower and the Secret Fan"** and **"The Tea Girl of Hummingbird Lane"**, Lisa See also explores Chinese culture and history in her works.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amy Tan's Influence:** Her novels have been translated into **more than 30 languages**, and she has received numerous awards for her contributions to literature.
 
• **The Joy Luck Club's Legacy:** The novel has been included in **school curriculums** and is celebrated as a significant work in American literature, particularly in the context of immigrant narratives.
 
• **Representation in Media:** The 1993 film adaptation helped increase the visibility of **Asian-American culture** in mainstream media, marking a milestone for diversity in Hollywood.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about India's population growth since 1981 and choose the correct option:

1. The rate of population growth began to decline gradually after 1981.

2. Birth rates continued to rise sharply in the 1990s.

3. Despite declining growth rate, 182 million people were added in the 1990s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1: The rate of population growth began to decline gradually after 1981** - This statement is **correct**. After 1981, India experienced a gradual decline in the population growth rate due to increased awareness about family planning, implementation of government policies, and socio-economic changes.
 
• **Statement 2: Birth rates continued to rise sharply in the 1990s**. This statement is **incorrect**. During the 1990s, birth rates in India began to decline as a result of better healthcare, education, and family planning measures.
 
• **Statement 3: Despite the declining growth rate, 182 million people were added in the 1990s**. This statement is **correct**. Even though the growth rate was declining, the population base was already large, leading to the addition of 182 million people in the 1990s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Population Growth in India:**

 
 
• India's population growth peaked during the 1960s and 1970s, primarily due to high birth rates and declining death rates as a result of improvements in healthcare and sanitation.
 
• Since 1981, the growth rate has been declining due to better family planning and awareness initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Factors Contributing to Declining Growth Rates:**
 
 
• Increased literacy rates, especially among women.
 
• Government initiatives like the National Population Policy (2000) aimed at stabilizing the population.
 
• Access to contraceptives and better healthcare services.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Despite Decline:**
 
 
• India's population remains one of the largest in the world, contributing to challenges like urban overcrowding, unemployment, and resource depletion.
 
• The demographic dividend of a young population requires sustainable policies in education, skill development, and employment.
 
 
 
• **Key Population Statistics:**
 
 
• India added approximately 181 million people between 1991 and 2001, despite a declining growth rate.
 
• The total fertility rate (TFR) in India has been steadily decreasing. As of the latest estimates, it is nearing the replacement level of 2.1.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Population Policy (2000):**

 
 
• Aimed at achieving population stabilization by 2045.
 
• Key goals include reducing the infant mortality rate to below 30 per 1,000 live births and achieving universal access to contraception.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Transition in India:**
 
 
• India is currently in the third stage of demographic transition, characterized by declining birth and death rates.
 
• With continuous efforts, India is expected to achieve replacement-level fertility soon.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• India is expected to surpass China as the most populous country by the late 2020s, according to United Nations projections.
 
• Despite the challenges, India’s demographic dividend offers significant potential for economic growth if harnessed effectively.

• Other important oil fields in Assam include **Rudrasagar, Moran, and Naharkatiya**.
 
• The state is also home to natural gas fields and supports several refineries, such as the **Numaligarh Refinery**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Assam-Arakan Basin** is considered one of India’s oldest and most important sedimentary basins for hydrocarbon exploration.
 
• Digboi’s development marked the beginning of India’s **petroleum industry**, which has since expanded to other regions such as Gujarat, Rajasthan, and offshore fields in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesized by intestinal microbiota?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin K**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin K** is a fat-soluble vitamin primarily involved in the process of blood clotting, enabling the body to prevent excessive bleeding.
 
• The **intestinal microbiota**, especially bacteria in the large intestine, synthesize Vitamin K naturally in the human body.
 
• Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of certain proteins that are required for blood coagulation and bone metabolism.
 
• Although dietary sources like green leafy vegetables, broccoli, and liver provide Vitamin K, a significant portion is generated internally by gut bacteria.
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin K can lead to issues such as **excessive bleeding (hemorrhaging)** as the blood's clotting ability is impaired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vitamin K forms:**

 
 
• Vitamin K exists in two main forms: **K1 (phylloquinone)** and **K2 (menaquinone)**.
 
• Vitamin K1 is obtained from plant sources like spinach, kale, and broccoli, while Vitamin K2 is synthesized by gut bacteria and is also found in animal-based foods and fermented products.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Vitamin K:**
 
 
• It plays a crucial role in the synthesis of proteins required for blood clotting, particularly **prothrombin**.
 
• Vitamin K also contributes to maintaining bone health by regulating calcium deposition, reducing the risk of osteoporosis.
 
 
 
• **Other vitamins in context:**
 
 
• **Vitamin C:** A water-soluble vitamin known for its antioxidant properties and its role in boosting immunity.
 
• **Vitamin D:** A fat-soluble vitamin responsible for calcium absorption and bone health, synthesized in the skin upon exposure to sunlight.
 
• **Vitamin E:** Another fat-soluble vitamin acting as an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.
 
 
 
• **Gut microbiota and Vitamin K:**
 
 
• The human gut hosts a variety of bacteria, including **Bacteroides** and **Escherichia coli**, that produce Vitamin K2 as a by-product of their metabolic processes.
 
• This symbiotic relationship is essential for meeting the body's Vitamin K requirements, especially when dietary intake is insufficient.
 
 
 
• **Clinical importance:**
 
 
• Newborns are at risk of Vitamin K deficiency because their gut microbiota is not fully developed. Hence, they are often given a Vitamin K injection soon after birth to prevent bleeding disorders.
 
• In adults, long-term antibiotic use can disrupt gut bacteria, potentially leading to a temporary Vitamin K deficiency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Vitamin K:** It was first discovered in 1929 by Danish scientist **Henrik Dam**, who observed its role in blood coagulation.
 
• **Deficiency symptoms:** Apart from hemorrhaging, Vitamin K deficiency can lead to calcification of arteries and other soft tissues.
 
• **Daily requirements:** The recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for Vitamin K varies by age and gender. For adult men, it is **120 micrograms/day**, and for adult women, it is **90 micrograms/day**.
 
• **Therapeutic use:** Vitamin K supplements and injections are used to counteract blood-thinning medications like **warfarin** in case of overdose.

questions.question: Which scheme provides insurance to farmers against crop failure?

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** is a crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India on **13th January 2016** to provide comprehensive insurance coverage to farmers against crop failure due to non-preventable natural calamities.
 
• The scheme aims to **stabilize farmers' income**, ensure the continuity of farming, and encourage farmers to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices.
 
• Farmers are required to pay a **minimal premium rate** of 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops, with the remaining premium being subsidized by the government.
 
• **Coverage:** The scheme covers risks such as drought, flood, hailstorm, cyclone, pest infestation, and other similar non-preventable risks.
 
• The scheme is implemented through **private and public insurance companies** under the coordination of state governments and financial institutions, ensuring a seamless claim settlement process for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Launched in **2007**, RKVY aims to achieve 4% annual growth in agriculture by providing financial assistance to states for agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• It is a flexible and state-driven scheme that incentivizes states to increase investment in agriculture and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM):**
 
 
• Launched in **2014-15**, SMAM focuses on promoting agricultural mechanization to increase productivity and reduce labor dependency.
 
• It provides subsidies for the purchase of agricultural machinery and implements, particularly for small and marginal farmers.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF):**
 
 
• Introduced in **2020**, AIF aims to provide medium to long-term debt financing for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
 
• It is a part of the government's Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan to strengthen agriculture infrastructure and supply chains.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of PMFBY:**
 
 
• It integrates technology like **remote sensing, GPS, and drones** for faster and more accurate assessment of crop loss.
 
• The scheme ensures **timely claim settlement**, with claims disbursed to the farmers' bank accounts directly.
 
• Coverage extends to **post-harvest losses** due to cyclones and unseasonal rains.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **National Crop Insurance Portal** is the digital platform for PMFBY, allowing farmers to register and track claims online.
 
• PMFBY is applicable to **loanee farmers** (those who take loans from financial institutions) and non-loanee farmers.
 
• The scheme was revised in **2020** to make it voluntary for farmers and to address regional disparities in insurance coverage.
 
• It is considered the **world’s largest crop insurance scheme** based on farmer participation and coverage.

questions.question:
Read the following statements and select the appropriate options:

**Statement 1:** A budget deficit is encountered when the total expenditure of the government is greater than its total revenue, excluding borrowings.

**Statement 2:** A budget deficit is faced when the total revenue of the government is greater than its expenditure in a fiscal year.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A budget deficit is encountered when the **total expenditure of the government exceeds its total revenue, excluding borrowings**. This definition aligns with the economic concept of a budget deficit. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 2:** This statement incorrectly reverses the concept of a budget deficit. If the total revenue of the government is greater than its expenditure, it results in a budget surplus, not a deficit. *Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• A **budget deficit** occurs when the government’s expenditure on services, infrastructure, and other public sector needs surpasses its revenue collections (excluding borrowing).
 
• A common source of revenue for governments includes **taxation, non-tax revenues, and dividends**, whereas expenditures include welfare programs, salaries, interest payments, and infrastructure spending.
 
• To cover a budget deficit, governments often rely on borrowing, which may take the form of issuing bonds or loans from domestic and international markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Budget Deficits:**

 
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** It occurs when the government’s total revenue receipts are less than its revenue expenditures.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** This is the total borrowing requirement of the government. It is calculated as the difference between total expenditure and total receipts (excluding borrowings).
 
• **Primary Deficit:** This is the fiscal deficit excluding interest payments on previous borrowings. It reflects the current year's borrowing needs.
 
 
 
• **Impacts of a Budget Deficit:**
 
 
• Governments may resort to borrowing, leading to an increase in public debt.
 
• Excessive deficits can lead to inflation if financed by printing money.
 
• In the long term, persistent deficits may lead to economic instability.
 
 
 
• **Budget Surplus:** A budget surplus occurs when the government’s total revenue exceeds its total expenditure in a fiscal year. This allows governments to reduce debt or invest in infrastructure.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• India often reports fiscal deficits in its Union Budget, reflecting the need for borrowing to fund development and welfare programs.
 
• Countries such as Germany and Switzerland have occasionally achieved budget surpluses due to high revenues and controlled expenditures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Budget:** A government budget is an annual financial statement presenting its anticipated revenue and expenditure for the coming fiscal year.
 
• **Fiscal Responsibility:** Governments adopt fiscal responsibility laws, such as the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003,** in India, to ensure fiscal discipline.
 
• **Balanced Budget:** In a balanced budget, government revenues are equal to expenditures. While rare, such budgets are considered fiscally ideal for long-term stability.

• **Assertion (A):** Matangini Hazra did not die while participating in a Salt March in Odisha. This statement is **false**. Hazra was associated with the Quit India Movement, not the Salt March, and her death did not occur in Odisha.
 
• **Reason (R):** Matangini Hazra was shot by police while holding the national flag during the Quit India Movement. This statement is **true**. She died on September 29, 1942, during a procession at Tamluk, Bengal.

• **Matangini Hazra:**

 
 
• She was born on **19 October 1869** in a small village near Tamluk in Bengal.
 
• Hazra actively participated in the **Quit India Movement**, the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, and other protests against British rule.
 
• She earned the nickname "**Gandhi Buri**" (Old Lady Gandhi) for her commitment to Gandhian principles.
 
• She was shot dead while leading a procession with the Indian national flag and chanting "Vande Mataram."
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi on **8 August 1942**, it aimed at ending British rule in India.
 
• The movement's slogan was "**Do or Die**," urging Indians to fight for complete independence.
 
• It was marked by widespread protests, strikes, and acts of non-violent resistance, although it also witnessed instances of violence.
 
• While the movement was eventually suppressed, it intensified the demand for India's independence.
 
 
 
• **Salt March (Dandi March):**
 
 
• Led by Mahatma Gandhi in **1930**, it was a non-violent protest against the British salt tax.
 
• The march covered a distance of **240 miles**, starting from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat.
 
• It symbolized civil disobedience and inspired millions to join the freedom struggle.
 
• Matangini Hazra was not associated with this event; her contributions were later during the Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Tamluk Region:**
 
 
• Located in present-day **West Bengal**, it was a significant center of the Quit India Movement.
 
• The **National Government of Tamluk** was established in 1942 by freedom fighters as part of the movement.

• Her bravery and sacrifice are commemorated through various statues and memorials in Bengal.
 
• Schools and institutions have been named after her to honor her contributions to India's freedom struggle.

• Women like **Sarojini Naidu, Kasturba Gandhi, Aruna Asaf Ali**, and Matangini Hazra played crucial roles in mobilizing mass participation.
 
• Their involvement demonstrated the inclusive nature of the freedom struggle and inspired future generations.

**Assertion (A):** The planning approach between 1951-1990 led to a successful transformation of India's employment structure.

**Reason (R):** Over 65% of India's workforce remained dependent on agriculture during this period.

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** The statement that "The planning approach between 1951-1990 led to a successful transformation of India's employment structure" is **false**. During this period, India's employment structure remained largely dependent on agriculture, with limited success in transitioning the workforce into industrial or service sectors.
 
• **Reason (R):** The statement "Over 65% of India's workforce remained dependent on agriculture during this period" is **true**. Even after several five-year plans emphasizing industrialization and economic reforms, the reliance on agriculture as the primary source of employment persisted.
 
• The planning approach between 1951 and 1990 aimed at economic growth, industrialization, and self-reliance, but was unable to significantly alter the employment structure due to factors such as lack of infrastructure, slow industrial growth, and inadequate skill development.
 
• The workforce during this period faced challenges in transitioning to non-agricultural sectors as agriculture remained the backbone of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Planning in India (1951-1990):**

 
 
• The first five-year plan (1951-1956) focused on **agriculture and infrastructure development** to revive the economy post-independence.
 
• Subsequent plans emphasized industrialization, including the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, which adopted the Nehru-Mahalanobis model focusing on heavy industries.
 
• Despite efforts, the **industrial sector's growth** was insufficient to absorb the growing workforce, leaving the majority reliant on agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Employment Challenges:**
 
 
• During 1951-1990, India faced issues like **population growth**, lack of education, and inadequate skill development, which hindered employment diversification.
 
• Unorganized sectors like agriculture continued to dominate, with **low productivity and disguised unemployment**.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture's Dominance:**
 
 
• Agriculture employed **more than 65% of India's workforce**, contributing to a significant portion of GDP during the planning era.
 
• Efforts like the **Green Revolution** in the 1960s improved productivity but did not significantly reduce agricultural dependency.
 
 
 
• **Post-1990 Reforms:**
 
 
• India saw a shift in employment structure post-1990 due to economic liberalization, globalization, and industrial growth.
 
• Sectors like **information technology** and services began to absorb a larger share of the workforce, reducing reliance on agriculture.

• **Employment Data:** By the end of 1990, agriculture contributed significantly to employment, but industrial and service sectors began showing growth.
 
• **Economic Reforms:** Post-1991 reforms led to liberalization, privatization, and globalization, significantly altering India's employment dynamics.

questions.question: Which global body promotes liberal economic reforms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IMF**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is an international organization established in **1944** at the Bretton Woods Conference and officially came into existence on **27th December 1945**.
 
• The primary objective of the IMF is to promote **global economic stability** by fostering **liberal economic reforms**, monetary cooperation, balanced economic growth, and financial stability among its member countries.
 
• IMF works to **liberalize economies** by advocating for free-market policies, reducing trade barriers, and providing financial support to countries in economic distress to ensure economic liberalization and structural reforms.
 
• The IMF provides **policy advice**, financial assistance, and technical expertise to its 190 member countries to strengthen their economies, reduce poverty, and achieve sustainable economic growth.
 
• It plays a critical role in international monetary systems, offering loans to countries facing **balance-of-payment crises** and ensuring the smooth functioning of global financial markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions of the IMF:**

 
 
• The IMF provides **financial assistance** to member countries experiencing economic difficulties by offering loans to stabilize their economies.
 
• It monitors global economic trends and provides **policy advice** to countries on fiscal, monetary, and financial issues to ensure economic stability.
 
• It encourages international trade by promoting **free-market policies** and reducing trade restrictions.
 
• The IMF offers **technical assistance** and training to member nations in areas such as public finance management, monetary policy, exchange rate policies, and financial sector reforms.
 
• It works closely with other international organizations like the World Bank to address global economic challenges.
 
 
 
• **IMF’s Role in Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• IMF promotes **liberalization** of economies by advising countries to reduce subsidies, privatize state-owned enterprises, and reform tax systems to boost economic growth.
 
• It advocates for **structural adjustment programs** that encourage countries to implement fiscal discipline, reduce inflation, and foster open trade policies.
 
• IMF's policies often emphasize the importance of developing **market-driven economies** to enhance global integration.
 
• Many countries have successfully implemented IMF-recommended reforms to stabilize their economies and attract foreign investment.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Other Options:**
 
 
• **UNDP:** The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** focuses on sustainable development, poverty eradication, and reducing inequalities rather than promoting liberal economic reforms.
 
• **WHO:** The **World Health Organization (WHO)** primarily works on global health issues and does not engage in economic reforms.
 
• **UNESCO:** The **United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)** focuses on education, culture, science, and communication, not economic reforms.
 
 
 
• **IMF in Numbers:**
 
 
• The IMF has **190 member countries** as of **2023**.
 
• The organization’s headquarters is located in **Washington, D.C., USA**.
 
• The total financial resources of the IMF amount to approximately **1 trillion SDRs** (Special Drawing Rights), which is equivalent to about **$1.3 trillion USD**.
